connections.label: key and config by Bitwarden Send

cards.title: Once: get access
items: The administrator adds you to the stage file and deploys the stage
You get one key and one client config through a Bitwarden Send
Store the key in ~/.aws/credentials under the profile name of the config
Save the config as ~/.config/agentcore-memory/config.json; it holds no key
Set AGENTCORE_PROJECT to your project: the config names no Git remote or folder

cards.title: Each day: what you type
items: Start Pi with the AgentCore extension, or claude --plugin-dir packages/agentcore-claude

Type a prompt: the client first recalls /shared/, /actor// and /project/

/shared/
Ask the agent to remember a fact: it proposes it and writes only after you say yes
Copy a file: aws s3 cp <file> s3://<bucket>/users/<you>/ --profile <profile>
Stop every memory call: AGENTCORE_MEMORY_DISABLE=1

cards.title: Maintainers review
items:
agentcore-memory proposals list --project

--actor

agentcore-memory proposals approve --project

--actor --id

An approved fact moves to /project/

/shared/, and each member then recalls it

A rejected fact moves to /project/

/rejected//

cards.title: What the rules refuse
items: The records and the files of another person
A project of which you are no member
Your own write into project shared: a maintainer approves it
A delete of a memory record, and a delete in a project folder

cards.title: What costs money
items: AgentCore Memory meters stored records and retrieval requests; each recall sends retrievals
The stage bucket: the stored files and the requests
Your IAM user and its key cost nothing
Not verified: the rates; read the AgentCore pricing page

cards.title: Proven and not verified
items: Proven on the dev stage: the deploy, one key for each user and 49 live access cases
Not verified: the tenant-pi client against a stage of this design
Not verified: the Bitwarden Send hand-over, offboarding and key rotation
